prompt:
Complete `VksClusterApplyClient.java` as a dependency-free, single-file Java 17 client for one VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 integration workflow: validate a vSphere Supervisor namespace through vCenter, then server-side apply a VKS Cluster object through the Supervisor Kubernetes API. The mutating request must be safe to replay after its response stream is lost, without provisioning a second Cluster or applying the desired state twice.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused vCenter contract was projected directly from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26`. The YAML specification, not a rendered documentation page, is the vCenter wire authority. The exact VMware operationId in scope is `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_getV2`. The VKS route is separately labeled as a native Kubernetes resource operation and deliberately has an operation key rather than a fictional VMware operationId.

Preserve every public record, exception type, accessor, and method signature already declared in `VksClusterApplyClient.java`. Use only the Java 17 standard library and do not add another production source file.

Construction performs no traffic. Both endpoint values must be absolute HTTP(S) origins with no user information, non-root path, query, fragment, or forced query. Both credentials must be nonblank and contain no CR or LF, and the timeout must be positive. The client must use an independent `HttpClient` that never follows redirects.

`apply(ApplyRequest)` validates all required strings before traffic. Control-plane replicas must be positive; an optional worker replica count must be nonnegative; CIDR lists and their elements must be non-null and every CIDR element must be nonblank. `workerReplicas == null`, empty CIDR lists, and `force == null` mean unset.

First invoke `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_getV2` exactly once with a bodyless `GET /api/vcenter/namespaces/instances/v2/{namespace}`. Require exactly HTTP 200 and a valid `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances.InfoV2` JSON object, including every required field and every required `stats` member. Its `supervisor` must exactly match the request. Recognize only `CONFIGURING`, `REMOVING`, `RUNNING`, and `ERROR`; only `RUNNING` may continue. A recognized non-running status returns `NamespaceNotReadyException`; malformed or unknown success data returns `ProtocolException`.

Then invoke native operation `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2:namespaced-clusters:server-side-apply` with `PATCH /apis/cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2/namespaces/{namespace}/clusters/{clusterName}`. Send exactly one `fieldManager` query value. Include `force=true` or `force=false` only when `force` is non-null. Omit `dryRun`, `fieldValidation`, `pretty`, and all other unset query fields instead of sending empty values or a bare delimiter. Use exact content type `application/apply-patch+yaml`; compact UTF-8 JSON is the apply-patch body and is valid YAML.

The body property order is `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata`, then `spec`. Metadata contains only `name` and `namespace`. Spec contains `topology`, then optional `clusterNetwork`. Topology contains `class`, `version`, the `vmClass` and `storageClass` variables in that order, `controlPlane`, and optional `workers`. Control plane contains only `replicas`. When worker replicas are set, workers contains one `machineDeployments` item with exactly `class: node-pool`, `name: worker`, and `replicas`, preserving explicit zero. Include `clusterNetwork` only when at least one CIDR list is nonempty; inside it include `pods` before `services`, and each present member contains only `cidrBlocks`. Do not send status, uid, resourceVersion, generation, labels, annotations, nulls, empty arrays, empty objects, or other placeholders.

Require exactly HTTP 200 from apply and validate the returned Cluster API version, kind, name, namespace, nonblank uid and resourceVersion, and positive integral generation. Return those values plus the number of PATCH attempts.

The first PATCH may have committed before its response stream fails. If that first attempt ends in an `IOException`, replay the same immutable `HttpRequest` exactly once. Do not rebuild its URI, headers, or body and do not repeat the namespace GET. Server-side apply sets desired state for a stable namespace, Cluster name, and field manager, so this byte-identical replay must not create or append another effect. Never retry an HTTP response, an oversized or malformed success, a validation failure, or a second transport failure; never send more than two PATCH attempts. Preserve interruption and keep all errors free of credentials, response bodies, decoded server messages, and lower-level transport text.

The request wire is strict. Percent-encode every dynamic path or query value as opaque UTF-8 RFC 3986 data. Every request sends exactly one `Accept: application/json`. Send exactly one `vmware-api-session-id` only to vCenter and exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <token>` only to Kubernetes. GET has no body, Content-Type, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, query, or bare `?`. PATCH has the exact content type, known Content-Length, and no Transfer-Encoding. Do not follow redirects. Preserve non-success operation, status, and a defensively copied response body through `ApiException` accessors while keeping its message sanitized.

Acceptance is `python3 -B .moonshiner/verify.py`. The protected verifier compiles with `javac --release 17`, exercises the single client through `TestMain`, starts the supplied contract-pinned mock only on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, and reads its synchronized, flushed request log. The mock derives its complete two-route allow-list from `docs/contract.json`, serves only those operations, commits the first ambiguous PATCH before truncating its response, and counts an identical replay as the same effect. If the execution sandbox forbids listener creation, the harness uses the same contract-derived behavior and request-log format through an in-process exchange. Runtime cases verify exact methods, raw targets, headers, byte-exact bodies and property order, optional-field omission, explicit zero and false preservation, immutable retry bytes, one-effect replay, redirect refusal, readiness gating, and validation before I/O. No live VMware or Kubernetes endpoint is contacted.

`TestMain.java`, `.moonshiner/verify.py`, `tools/contract_mock.py`, and everything under `docs/` are protected; edit only `VksClusterApplyClient.java`.

research.product: VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 vSphere Supervisor and VKS
research.interface: vSphere Automation REST plus native Kubernetes Cluster API
research.language_rationale: The task exercises dependency-free Java HTTP composition, strict JSON and REST wire handling, cross-control-plane authentication, optional-field semantics, and safe replay of an ambiguous desired-state mutation.
